questions.body: What comes next in the sequence: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by two each time: 4, 6, 8, 10, then 12. So 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.body: All Bloops are Razzies. All Razzies are Lazzies. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The relation chains one way only: Bloops sit inside Razzies, which sit inside Lazzies. Nothing is claimed about the reverse direction.

questions.body: What is 15% of 240?
questions.explanation: 10% is 24 and 5% is 12, so 15% is 36.

questions.body: The average of 5 numbers is 20. If the number 30 is removed, what is the average of the remaining 4?
questions.explanation: The total is 5 x 20 = 100. Removing 30 leaves 70 across 4 numbers, so 17.5.

questions.body: Three workers build a wall in 12 days. Working at the same rate, how long would four workers take?
questions.explanation: The job is 36 worker-days. Split across 4 workers that is 9 days.

questions.body: Which number does not belong: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11?
questions.explanation: Every other number is prime. 9 is 3 x 3.

questions.body: A shop raises a price by 20%, then offers 20% off the new price. Compared with the original, the final price is:
questions.explanation: 100 becomes 120, then 20% off 120 is 96. A percentage rise and the same percentage fall do not cancel.

questions.body: A 120 m long train travels at 60 km/h. Roughly how long does it take to pass a stationary pole?
questions.explanation: 60 km/h is about 16.7 m/s. 120 / 16.7 is about 7.2 seconds.

questions.body:
After this runs, what is sum?

sum = 0
for i in 1..5:
    sum = sum + i
questions.explanation: It adds 1 through 5, which is 15.

questions.body: Which data structure removes the most recently added item first?
questions.explanation: A stack is last-in, first-out. A queue is first-in, first-out.

questions.body: In most programming languages, the first element of an array is at index:
questions.explanation: Array indexing is zero-based in C, Java, Python, JavaScript, Go and most others.

options.body: It depends on the array length

questions.body: A boolean variable can hold:
questions.explanation: A boolean is a two-state value: true or false.

questions.body: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching an unsorted array of n items one by one?
questions.explanation: The target may be last or absent, so every one of the n items is checked.

questions.body: Binary search only works correctly when the data is:
questions.explanation: Each step discards half the range based on order, which requires the data to be sorted.

questions.body: Reading an array element by its index takes:
questions.explanation: The address is computed directly from the index, so it costs the same regardless of size.

options.body: Time proportional to the array length

questions.body: The main reason to put code in a function is to:
questions.explanation: Functions let one named, tested block be reused and changed in a single place.

options.body: Reuse it and keep changes in one place

questions.body: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1011?
One kilobyte is conventionally:
questions.explanation: Storage sizes are powers of two: 2^10 is 1024.

questions.body: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) average-case time?
questions.explanation: Merge sort splits and merges in O(n log n). Bubble, insertion and selection sort are O(n^2) on average.

questions.body: RAM is described as volatile memory because:
questions.explanation: Volatile means the contents need power to persist; they are lost when the machine is switched off.

options.body: Its contents are lost when power is removed
It can be written to only once
It is slower than a hard disk

questions.body: A compiler is best described as a program that:
questions.explanation: A compiler translates source code into another form, usually machine code, ahead of running it.

options.body: Runs source code one line at a time
Translates source code into machine code
Finds every bug in a program
Stores source code in a database

questions.body: Which of these is a markup language rather than a programming language?
questions.explanation: HTML describes the structure of a document. It has no variables, conditionals or loops.

questions.body:
How many times does this loop print?

i = 0
while i < 10:
    print(i)
    i = i + 2
questions.explanation: i takes the values 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8, then 10 fails the condition. That is 5 prints.

questions.body: A function calls itself with a smaller input until it reaches a base case. This technique is called:
questions.explanation: Recursion. Without a base case the calls never stop and the stack overflows.
